title: Workflow Automation Incident Analytics dashboard: access by workflow permission, time ranges, KPI tiles, triage and resolve times, and top-10 views

prose.text: {{what-it-is}} {{owner}} The Incidents page itself is in [[zwa.incidents]].

prose.label: Time range.
prose.text: {{time-range}} The Incidents page's equivalent range is in [[zwa.incidents:date-range]]. Retention beyond the six-month custom range and the time zone of ranges are not stated {{gap:range-details}}.

prose.label: Tiles and charts.
prose.text: {{summary-tiles}} The Response Available status is also held in [[zwa.incidents:status-widgets]]. {{triage-resolve}} {{status-and-trend}}

what-it-is.statement: The Incident Analytics dashboard (Analytics > Data Security > Incidents) gives high-level visibility into the organization's DLP incidents over a timeframe, such as the time taken to triage and resolve incidents, previous and current incident counts, and the cumulative number of new and resolved incidents.

quotes: The Incident Analytics dashboard gives high-level visibility and insight into your organization's Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incidents.
This dashboard provides a variety of information about the incidents over a specified timeframe
such as the time taken to triage and resolve incidents, previous and current incident counts, and the cumulative number of new and resolved incidents
On the Incident Analytics dashboard (Analytics > Data Security > Incidents), you can do the following:

owner.statement: The Workflow Automation 2024 release summary, in its January 18, 2024 entry, records that a new Incident Analytics page was added to the Workflow Automation Admin Portal; that is a dated release note, and the current dashboard page places the dashboard at Analytics > Data Security > Incidents. The Managing Incidents page points to the dashboard for DLP incident visibility.

quotes: A new Incident Analytics page is added to the Workflow Automation Admin Portal.
On the Incident Analytics dashboard (Analytics > Data Security > Incidents), you can do the following:
You can view high-level visibility and insight into your organization's Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incidents using the Incident Analytics dashboard.

workflow-access.statement: Admins with full workflow access can monitor all incidents in the organization and view the admins responsible for them; admins with restricted workflow access can only monitor the incidents assigned to them and cannot view incidents assigned to other admins. The table of DLP admins with the most incidents assigned is only available to admins with full workflow access permission.

quotes: admins with full workflow access can monitor all the incidents that have occurred in the organization and view the list of admins responsible for those incidents.
Admins with restricted workflow access can only monitor the incidents assigned to them.
They can't view the incidents assigned to other admins.
This table is only available to admins with full workflow access permission.

evidence.after: - New and Resolved Incidents Over Time
quotes: Top 10 DLP Admins
Displays a table listing the 10 DLP admins with the most incidents assigned to them.

export-pdf.statement: The dashboard exports to a PDF file, either everything available on the page or what the applied filter criteria show.

quotes: Export the incident analytics to a PDF file.
You can export all incident analytics available on the page, or use the filter criteria to modify the incident analytics displayed on the page and then export that information.

time-range.statement: By default the dashboard displays the current calendar week (Sunday through Saturday); the time range filter applies to all widgets and offers hour, day, week and month presets or a Custom Date Range with start and end dates and times, which only supports incidents up to 6 months old and a search window of at most 3 months.

quotes: By default, this page displays incident analytics for the current calendar week (Sunday through Saturday).
The time range filter applies to all widgets.

- Hours - Current Hour - Last Hour - Last 2 Hours - Last 6 Hours - Last 12 Hours - Days - Curent Day - Last Day - Weeks - Current Week - Last Week - Months - Current Month - Last Month - Custom Date Range
you can use the Custom Date Range option and specify the start and end dates and times
The Custom Date Range option only supports incidents that are up to 6 months old, and you can only search for a maximum of a 3-month window.

obfuscation.statement: If the User Name or Client IP attribute is chosen for obfuscation, the dashboard's incident data cannot be filtered using those obfuscated attributes.

quotes: If you choose the User Name attribute or Client IP attribute for obfuscation, you cannot filter the incident data on the dashboard using these obfuscated attributes.

summary-tiles.statement: Summary tiles give All (total incidents), Open and Resolved for the selected range, New and Resolved Incident Rate per day, and Response Available (incidents where a user or a manager or approver has responded, with the status Received Justification Response).

quotes: All: Displays the total number of incidents that have occurred in your organization.
Open: The number of open incidents for the selected time range.
Resolved: The number of resolved incidents for the selected time range.
New Incident Rate (Per Day): The rate of new incidents per day for the selected time range.
Resolved Incident Rate (Per Day): The rate of resolved incidents per day for the selected time range.

Response Available: The number of incidents where a user has provided a response from a user notification, or where a manager or approver has provided a response from an escalation notification (i.e., incidents with the status Received Justification Response).

triage-resolve.statement: Time to Triage is the time in hours from an incident's occurrence to its assignment to an admin, and Time to Resolve the time in hours for the admin to mark it resolved; the lighter blue bars show the previous time for the equivalent previous time range.

quotes: Time to Triage: The time taken in hours from the occurrence of an incident to its assignment to an admin.
Time to Resolve: The time taken in hours for the admin to mark an incident as resolved.
The lighter blue bars signify the previous incident time for incidents using the previous time range that is equivalent to the time range selected.

status-and-trend.statement: Incident by Status charts New, Open, Escalated and Resolved incidents, with darker blue bars for the current count and lighter blue bars for the previous count; a Pareto chart shows the new incident count with the cumulative new and cumulative resolved incident counts.

quotes: Displays a bar chart of incidents by their status for the selected time range. The chart shows the following statuses:
- New - Open - Escalated - Resolved
the darker blue bars signify the current incident count, and the lighter blue bars signify the previous incident count
Displays a Pareto chart with the number of new and resolved incidents for the selected time range.
- New Incident Count - Cumulative New Incident Count - Cumulative Resolved Incident Count

top-10-lists.statement: Top 10 lists cover the most violated DLP policy rules and DLP dictionaries, and the DLP policy rules and dictionaries with the largest number of resolved incidents marked as false positives.

quotes: Displays a list of the 10 most violated DLP policy rules with the DLP rule name and the number of incidents generated against each rule.
Displays a list of the 10 most violated DLP dictionaries
Displays a list of the 10 DLP policy rules with the largest number of resolved incidents that are marked as false positives for each rule.
Displays a list of the 10 DLP dictionaries with the largest number of resolved incidents that are marked as false positives for each dictionary.

top-10-admins-users.statement: Top 10 DLP Admins lists the 10 admins with the most incidents assigned to them (login ID, new and resolved incidents, average resolution time in hours); Top 10 Users lists end users by email with total, new, escalated, critical and high incidents, and clicking a user email opens the Incidents page showing that end user's incidents, with other applied filters kept.

quotes: Displays a table listing the 10 DLP admins with the most incidents assigned to them.
Assigned Admin: The login ID for the admin.
New Incidents: The number of incidents with new status assigned to the admin.
Resolved Incidents: The number of incidents that the admin has resolved.
Average Resolution Time (Hours): The average time in hours that the admin took to resolve an incident.
Displays a table listing the 10 DLP end users with the most incidents associated with them.
User Email: The email ID of the end user.
Total Incidents: The total number of incidents associated with the end user.
New Incidents: The number of incidents with new status associated with the end user.
Escalated Incidents: The number of incidents escalated to the end user's manager or approver.
Critical Incidents: The number of critical priority incidents associated with the end user.
High Incidents: The number of high-severity incidents associated with the end user.
When you click the user email link, you are redirected to the Incidents page, which displays only the incidents created by that end user.
If you applied other filters before clicking the user email link, those filters remain applied, as well.

range-details.title: Incident Analytics retention, time zone, PDF export and the Open tile
range-details.detail: The page states no retention beyond the 6-month custom range and no time zone for ranges. It does not say whether the PDF export honours obfuscation, or how the Open tile is counted; the Incidents page defines Open for its own widgets.
